newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ENDEMOL PLAYS DOWN GERMAN SETBACK REPORT.
newsitem.headline: ENDEMOL PLAYS DOWN GERMAN SETBACK REPORT.

text.p: Television and theatre producer Endemol Entertainment NV on Thursday played down a report in newspaper De Telegraaf which said Endemol was about to suffer a severe blow in its German television market.
"The headline is total nonsense and the story is premature to say the least," spokesman Thomas Notermans told Reuters.

The newspaper said in its headline Endemol was about to lose its German market. It continued by saying Endemol was in talks on a new contract with German broadcaster RTL Television and might lose tens of millions of guilders compared with the previous three-year deal which brought in about 200 million.
Notermans said Endemol had just started negotiations with RTL Television, in which Luxembourg's Audiofina and Germany's Bertelsmann have stakes.
"It is quite common to enter such negotiations in a rather tough way and that is exactly what happened," Notermans said.

He added that RTL Television had just aired a television film made by Endemol as its "movie of the week" which had become the best scoring film in terms of viewer numbers in the broadcaster's history. The station had already said it definitely wanted more of these films, Notermans said.
The spokesman said Endemol's other German business was also doing quite well. In March it took a 49 percent stake in Munich-based tv-producer GAT, which showed good prospects.
Endemol is also about to produce Bild TV five times per week, a television version of the German mass-circulation daily newspaper Bild Zeitung.
Notermans said the Bild contract would bring in "substantial" turnover volumes but declined to specify further financial details of the contract.
